user_reported_bug: nao me deixa importar de novo os ficheiros porque ja foram carregados
summary: No relevant testing skill found. Backend-only retest confirmed the main bypass case now works: a file hash with only an old imported silent-zero record is accepted and applies data (HTTP 200). Regression pytest suite passed 34/34. However, a real API edge case remains: after the allowed reimport creates a useful imported record with the same hash, uploading the same file again still returns HTTP 200 instead of blocking because duplicate detection uses an arbitrary find_one by file_hash and can keep seeing the older silent-zero record. This means the hash-check fix is incomplete for the reimport flow once multiple records share the hash.

critical.issue: Duplicate hash blocking is incomplete when both an old silent-zero import and a newer useful import share the same file_hash. Reproduction via /app/test_reports/iter49_api_edge_test.py: seed old status=imported/totals=0 client_info import, first upload returns 200 and applies clients_updated=1, second upload of the same file also returns 200 instead of HTTP 400. The same_hash_imports output shows three imported records with the same hash.

action_items: In upload_import duplicate detection, search for any useful prior import for the same file_hash (status imported/accepted_with_warnings plus applied counters >0) before allowing bypass; do not rely on an unsorted find_one that may return an old silent-zero record.
Add a regression test for the exact sequence: old silent-zero same hash -> first reimport accepted/applies data -> immediate second upload of same file blocked with HTTP 400 'já foi importado'.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/modules/finance/routes.py lines 1925-1956 uses db.finance_imports.find_one({'file_hash': file_hash}) with no sort and no useful-status/applied filter. Since file_hash is not unique, once a silent-zero record and a useful reimport both exist, Mongo may return the silent-zero record and permanently bypass duplicate blocking for that hash.

Script dry-run was executed and created /tmp/finance_silent_zero_backup_20260725T113404Z.json without DB changes; current DB had 0 matching silent-zero candidates at that moment. Existing pytest covers --confirm preservation behavior. No APIs were MOCKED.
seed_data_creation: Created temporary BUG49QA finance_client and old silent-zero finance_import directly in Mongo for API reproduction; script cleaned up BUG49QA imports/files/client afterward. Regression pytest created/cleaned its own TSTHB49 data.

Services were running. git status showed modified backend/modules/finance/routes.py and new backend/scripts/mark_silent_zero_imports.py and backend/tests/test_iteration_49_hash_bypass.py. Pytest command `python -m pytest tests/test_iteration_43_open_docs_safety_guards.py tests/test_iteration_44_overdue_safety_guards.py tests/test_iteration_46_import_preview.py tests/test_iteration_46b_detect_type.py tests/test_iteration_47_anomalies.py tests/test_iteration_48_infoclientes_evolucao.py tests/test_iteration_49_hash_bypass.py -q` passed 34/34. Direct API evidence: first upload after silent-zero returned 200 with clients_updated=1; second same-hash upload also returned 200, which is the remaining failure.
rca_of_the_issue: The surgical bypass correctly distinguishes a single old silent-zero record from a useful import, but it only evaluates one arbitrary finance_imports document for the hash. With no unique index on file_hash, successful reimport creates a second same-hash record. Future duplicate checks can still read the older silent-zero record and allow unlimited reimports, instead of blocking because a useful imported record now exists.
